companyDescription: Multi-domain autonomous defense platform · Sentrycs C-UAS + Lockheed Sanctum · $390M FY2026 guidance · $457M backlog
priceNote: 52% below 52-wk high $15.28 — Sentrycs+Lockheed integration ongoing; Cyberhawk acquisition closing Q3
summary: Ondas transformed from a small SDR company into a multi-domain autonomous defense platform through 6 acquisitions in 2026. Q1 2026 revenue was $50.1M (+1,079% YoY), FY2026 guided at $390M. Sentrycs C-UAS is now integrated into Lockheed Martin's Sanctum platform and 8 analyst consensus targets average $19.83 — implying +140% upside. Q2 already has $150M+ in orders with Q2 earnings mid-August being the next major catalyst.

catalysts.name: Sentrycs + Lockheed Martin Sanctum Integration
catalysts.description: Sentrycs' Cyber-over-RF C-UAS tech integrated into Lockheed's Sanctum C2 platform (announced Jun 23). Prime defense validator — now part of Lockheed's standard counter-drone architecture.

catalysts.name: Cyberhawk Acquisition Close
catalysts.description: $125M acquisition of Cyberhawk — AI-enabled drone inspection for critical infrastructure (power lines, pipelines, telecom towers). Closes Q3 2026. Opens non-defense revenue stream.

catalysts.name: Q2 2026 Earnings
catalysts.description: Q2 orders already $150M+ (vs Q1 $50.1M). $390M FY guidance requires back-half ramp — Q2 report will show if revenue is converting from backlog. Watch gross margin (~49% in Q1).

catalysts.name: $4.3B DoD/NATO Pipeline
catalysts.description: 45+ global program submissions; 1M active C-UAS programs in 2026 per company data. LADOS C2 debuted at Eurosatory 2026 — potential NATO contract anchor.

risks: Severe share dilution — shares outstanding grew 352% in 12 months; ATM and acquisition stock payments ongoing
Negative operating cash flow — burned $38.7M in FY2025; Q1 2026 shows improvement but still pre-positive FCF
Acquisition integration risk — 6 acquisitions in 2026 (Sentrycs, Mistral, World View, Omnisys, Cyberhawk) creates cultural + systems complexity
Defense budget risk — DOGE + Congressional reconciliation could slow DoD procurement timelines
Revenue concentration — $390M guidance depends on handful of large contracts; program delays = guidance miss
Prospectus for resale of shares filed — overhang from recent acquisition-linked equity

estimateDates.note: Q2 orders already $150M+; key read on $390M FY guidance conversion and gross margin
$125M cash deal — adds AI drone inspection for critical infrastructure

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed at 3.50–3.75%; government defense contracts are rate-insensitive. ONDS revenue is DoD/NATO contract-driven — decoupled from rate cycle.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Core PCE 3.4% (3-yr high); defense contract inflation adjustments protect margins. Input cost (electronics, components) is the primary inflation exposure.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: Iran conflict + Ukraine + NATO C-UAS spending = secular tailwind for ONDS. Defense budgets are rising globally — DOGE risk is DoD-specific program delays, not sector contraction.
macroRisk.summary: LOW — government contract base is rate/inflation-insulated. Primary risks are execution (6 acquisitions) and dilution, not macro.

catalystSpot.preRunup: Defense contract announcements and partnership confirmations (Lockheed, Palantir, World View) historically drive 10-20% single-session moves in ONDS. The stock has been in consolidation post-$15 high — each new contract = re-rating pop.

postWin.note: Q1 2026 earnings beat sent stock +26.5% next day. Lockheed partnership announcement: +15% near-term. Defense contract announcements: +10-20% on the day.

postLose.note: Revenue miss vs $390M guidance or dilutive equity offering = significant de-rating. Stock already -46% from 52-wk high shows the downside pattern.

spotSizing.reason: High analyst consensus upside (+140%) but severe dilution risk (352% share count increase) + pre-FCF positive. Speculative sizing — 3-4% max; scale in on dips.

stopPreCatalyst.note: Below Jun support = dilution announcement or contract delay

stopPostCatalyst.note: If Q2 earnings show revenue below $80M or $390M FY guide cut, exit within 2 sessions
